newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-DECIMATED BARCELONA FACE TEST AGAINST FIORENTINA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DECIMATED BARCELONA FACE TEST AGAINST FIORENTINA.

text.p: A Barcelona squad that is arguably the strongest in Europe will be stretched to the limits on Thursday in the first leg of their Cup Winner's Cup semifinal with Italy's Fiorentina.
Three-times winners Barcelona will be without six players, four of them instant first choices.

Barcelona warmed up for the game by thrashing Sporting Gijon 4-0 over the weekend and were boosted by the news that both their chief rivals for second place in the Spanish league and leaders Real Madrid were held to draws.
But seven points still separate Barcelona from their arch-rivals and coach Bobby Robson knows that his main chance of serving out the second year of his contract lies in taking a European title.
Barcelona won the Cup Winners' Cup in 1979, 1982 and 1989 but Fiorentina are far from overawed by their reputation.
Their Argentine striker Gabriel Batistuta said: "I've
never felt inferior to anyone. Sure the Catalan side has 22 great players and lots of international experience but the real Fiorentina can beat any side."
Fiorentina coach Claudio Ranieri believes it would be a major tactical error for his side to concentrate all their attention on Barcelona's Brazilian striker Ronaldo.
"That would be equivalent to allowing a free hand to all the other nine players, all equally useful," he said.
"Barcelona have too many star players and we cannot imagine that we can tie them all down. Our idea will be to tie up their overall gameplan and that will be the key to this match."
Fiorentina, who were unlucky in a 0-0 draw with Internazionale on Saturday, are currently ninth in Serie A, 17 points behind league leaders Juventus.
That lowly league standing reflects the extent to which the Florence club have based their whole season on their European campaign.
They will be handicapped by the absence of two first choice players in cuptied Russian winger Andreij Kanchelskis and suspended Swedish midfielder Stefan Schwarz.

Although coach Ranieri was giving nothing away on his plans, he may be tempted to play a cautious 4-5-1 formation to compensate for the loss of Schwarz's covering work and the extra width added by Kanchelskis.
Sandro Cois, Emiliano Bigica, Anselmo Robbiati and Brazilian Oliveira could all line up in midfield alongside Rui Costa, leaving Batistuta on his own up front.
As for Ronaldo, he may be marked in defence by Lorenzo Amoruso and in midfield by Cois.
Robson will be without key midfielders Ivan de la Pena and Josep Guardiola, both of whom are suspended.

Guardiola and de la Pena tend to supply the ideas, while injuries have put paid to the two Barcelona men best known for their commitment and pace -- overlapping defender Sergi Barjuan and utility man Luis Enrique Martinez.
Another midfielder, Oscar Garcia, is also out injured while winger Emmanuel Amunike is ineligible after turning out for Sporting Lisbon in a European competition already this season.
The game comes after a week in which Barcelona have been unnerved by the news linking Guardiola to Italy's Parma, while Lazio of Rome have expressed their interest in Ronaldo.
Probable teams:
Barcelona: Vitor Baia; Albert Ferrer, Abelardo Fernandez, Laurent Blanc, Miguel Angel Nadal; Gheorghe Popescu, Guillermo Amor, Giovanni; Hristo Stoichkov, Luis Figo, Ronaldo.
Fiorentina: Francesco Toldo; Guilio Falcone, Pasquale Padalino, Lorenzo Amoruso, Michele Serena; Oliveira, Emiliano Bigica, Sandro Cois, Anselmo Robbiati, Rui Costa; Gabriel Batistuta.
